prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] Code · CLI flags (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Flag" · longest unbreakable word 106px · one-line width 204px
  col 2: header "Type" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 55px
  col 3: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 114px · one-line width 114px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 89px · one-line width 477px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 625px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 624px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A compact reference for CLI flags, their value types, defaults, and effects.","reading":"Readers locate a flag, then scan across its row to check its type, default, and description; they may also compare defaults or types down a column.","groups":["Flag, Type, and Default define how each option is specified and what value it takes.","Description explains the effect of the flag and carries most of the prose."],"keep_intact":["Individual flag names and aliases","Type names","Default values, especially 127.0.0.1:9229"],"may_wrap":["Description prose at word boundaries","Multiple flag aliases between the aliases"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r1A: widths [218, 76, 135, 195] · table 625×345px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1B: widths [205, 76, 135, 208] · table 625×345px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r1C: widths [190, 76, 135, 223] · table 625×345px · row heights [36, 83, 83, 60, 83] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

The description column is also tight, producing short lines.","cause":"The 218px flag column provides 197px of text space, less than the 204px needed for the longest full flag content. Types and defaults remain legible.","problems":"The flag column is visibly cramped, with two identifiers split; the wider descriptions do not reduce the overall table height.","cause":"The 190px flag column leaves only 169px for text, while the 223px description column still leaves three descriptions at three lines."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"intact-flags","widths":[225,76,135,188],"change":"Give the flag column the 225px needed for its widest one-line content, keeping identifiers intact; retain the minimum widths needed for type and default values and give the remaining space to descriptions."},{"name":"flag-comfort","widths":[230,76,135,183],"change":"Add a small margin to the flag column to test whether slightly more breathing room improves the reference, accepting a narrower prose column."}]}
